Use case: precise-object-edit. Make only the specified corrections to the attached existing Episode08 Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature. Preserve its original figures, faces, poses, mineral tempera colors, patterned textiles, mountain fortress, soft vellum vignette and floral edge ornament. Preserve EXACT1586x992 pixel canvas and existing horizontal framing; no crop or size change.
1. The entire setting must be OUTDOORS on the rocky mountain battlefield of Khataeti, beneath the mountain fortress. Completely REMOVE the floating indoor blue-tiled palace arch, gold-filled arch opening and pale marble columns from the LEFT side behind mounted Tariel. Replace those architectural elements with continuous outdoor faceted ochre/lilac mountain rocks, open lapis-blue sky and sparse mountain cypress/pomegranate foliage, harmonizing with the existing ridges and fortress at right. There must be NO indoor palace arch, pavilion column, tiled room or interior wall remaining on the left. The distant mountain fortress on the upper right stays.
2. Change ONLY Tariel's large FOREGROUND horse from white/grey to a canonical JET-BLACK steed: deep lustrous black coat, black mane and black tail, black muzzle and legs, no white blaze or pale socks. Preserve the horse's posture, proportions and its existing elaborate blue/gold saddle cloth and jeweled bridle. The far-right background soldiers' horses can retain their current colors; do not confuse them with Tariel's black steed.
Keep Tariel in his pre-exile Indian military attire with no panther pelt, seated on the black horse; keep King Ramaz kneeling with lowered empty hands, his dropped sword and the three distant soldiers. Do not change their faces or add figures.
No text, letters, numbers, inscriptions, calligraphy, banners, flags, scrolls or watermarks anywhere. The correction must remain a soft-vignette medieval Georgian illuminated painting, not a photographic or modern digital scene. Exact native output1586x992.

attempts.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting illustrating Episode 8 of Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი): Expedition to Khataeti, Defeat of Ramaz & Victory Banquet.
Setting: Khataeti, the rocky mountain realm of King Ramaz, immediately after Tariel has overcome the ambush. A single coherent moment: the victorious young Tariel on his warhorse receives the defeated, dismounted Ramaz, who kneels with head inclined and hands open. Ramaz's surrendered sword rests safely on the ground. A few orderly soldiers and horses stand far behind them without flags; a mountain citadel and cypresses rise among rose-ochre faceted rocks. Victory rather than graphic battle is the subject. No feast or second scene.
Characters in scene: Tariel is a vigorous young Georgian-Eastern prince with olive skin, thick dark curly hair, strong brows and a dark beard matching reference 2. He wears fine Indian military armor, vermilion and gold textiles and a gold-trimmed cape; this early flashback PRECEDES his exile, so NO panther skin, NO fur hat and NO leopard cloak. Ramaz matches reference 3: stern middle-aged bearded king in an ornate pointed silver-and-gold helmet with cheekpieces and mail, golden shoulder armor and dark red garments. Preserve their distinct faces. Neither Parsadan nor Nestan is physically at this battlefield, so do not show them.
Input roles: reference 1 is STYLE ONLY, not its subject or setting; references 2 and 3 are Tariel and Ramaz IDENTITY ONLY, ignore their circular medallion frames. Show full scene figures, not portraits or medallions.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting for Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი). 16th–17th-century Georgian royal manuscript miniature, Mamuka Tavakarashvili / King Vakhtang VI illumination tradition blended with classical Persian-Safavid tempera miniature. Egg tempera, lapis lazuli, malachite green, vermilion, warm ochre and burnished antique gold leaf on aged ivory-parchment vellum. Stylized faceted rocky cliffs, ornamental cypress and pomegranate trees, intricately patterned arches and domes, expressive courtly figures in medieval Georgian-Eastern attire. Fine controlled contours, delicately patterned fabrics, luminous matte mineral pigments, slightly flattened layered miniature space with expressive narrative gestures. A painted manuscript scene, not photorealism, cinematic rendering, modern digital fantasy or a collage of circular portraits. Reuse referenced character faces and coloring but adapt costume to the actual chronological story scene; Tariel wears ordinary Indian court or military attire in early backstory, his panther skin belongs to his later exile. Exact horizontal 16:10 composition, preferably native 1600x1000 pixels, a single coherent scene framed for a card vignette. Soft natural painted vignette dissolving to warm aged ivory vellum at edges, modest antique-gold floral flourishes at the perimeter, no rigid border. Key faces and gestures comfortably inside the central safe area, no important content cut off. STRICTLY NO TEXT, NO LETTERS, NO CAPTIONS, NO NUMBERS, NO INSCRIPTIONS, NO CALLIGRAPHY, NO BANNERS, NO SCROLLS, NO SIGNATURES, NO WATERMARKS anywhere. Architectural ornament must be purely floral/geometric with no pseudo-writing. If letters are narratively necessary, use a small closed plain unmarked folded paper or sealed envelope, never visible writing or rolled scrolls. All book covers/pages must be plain and unmarked. Do not show graphic blood or gore; imply violent events through gestures, context and intact clothing.
Mandatory output: one horizontal 16:10 painting, preferably 1600x1000 native pixels. No wording from this prompt may appear in the artwork.
attempts.actual_scene: Tariel receives the defeated dismounted Ramaz in Khataeti after the ambush is overcome.
